memory_leads.lead: Ship repair and drydock begin with a defect, maintenance due item, survey/class requirement, planned upgrade or commercial conversion need. The trigger should remain distinct from the later approved work scope because discovery and inspection can materially expand or reduce what is actually done.

Technical management adds a project-owner layer between shipowner economics and yard execution: technical managers or superintendents can define worklists, gather maker/class input, tender work, supervise progress and recommend acceptance without becoming the legal shipowner or the yard.

A repair specification or worklist is a scoped procurement object. It translates observed defects, maintenance plans and upgrade goals into requested tasks, but it is not the same as the final completed-work record because quotations, exclusions and discovered conditions can alter scope.

Yard selection couples technical capability, berth/dock geometry, slot timing, geography, price expectation, supplier access and the vessel's trading schedule. A theoretically capable yard can still be unavailable if the required dock window or specialist resources are missing.

Arrival, deactivation, tank/space preparation, docking or safe positioning, opening-up and inspection form an execution transition before major work. A vessel can be physically at a yard yet not ready for every work package at the same time.

Steel, coating, machinery, propulsion, electrical, cargo-system and accommodation work are parallel work packages with different dependencies. Overall redelivery can be governed by a critical work package rather than average progress across the project.

Equipment makers, authorized or specialist service engineers, and spares/material suppliers create an external dependency layer. Repair duration can be extended by part identification, fabrication, transport, customs/logistics or specialist-attendance timing even when yard labor is available.

Opening machinery or structures can reveal discovered-condition work that was not visible when the initial specification was prepared. The resulting variation/change-order state separates original planned scope from newly authorized work and is a major route for schedule and cost uncertainty.

Conversion and regulatory retrofit projects differ from like-for-like repair because they change capability or compliance configuration: added or replaced equipment, structural modification, fuel/emissions systems or cargo-service conversion can require design, approval, integration and commissioning layers beyond routine maintenance.

Class, flag or other survey interfaces can create inspection/approval hold points during a project. Yard completion of physical work and external acceptance/verification are related but distinct states; a vessel may require evidence, tests or corrective work before release.

Testing and trials are staged evidence of readiness: dock tests, machinery/function tests, commissioning and sea-trial-type checks may detect unresolved defects. Passing one test does not imply that every system, class item or owner punch-list item is closed.

Acceptance, undocking/departure readiness, commercial redelivery and return to revenue service can occur on different clocks. Point-in-time capacity replay should distinguish physical departure from yard, contractual/project acceptance and actual availability for the next employment.

Repair-yard capacity and repair duration can temporarily remove meaningful fleet supply even when no vessel is scrapped. When many vessels require similar retrofits or survey work, constrained dock slots, service engineers or equipment can convert regulation and maintenance cycles into effective-capacity absorption.

P055 recycling memory is refined because repair-versus-demolition is not a static cost comparison: uncertain discovered work, yard-slot timing, parts availability, duration risk, test outcomes and expected post-repair earning life can change the decision after the vessel is already committed to inspection or yard work.

P053 survey memory is refined because condition observations can seed a repair worklist, while later opening-up and testing generate new observations; the project should preserve this sequence instead of rewriting the initial condition report with later findings.

Atlas regulation-as-supply memory is refined because retrofit requirements can absorb fleet capacity through design, equipment procurement, yard slots, installation and commissioning before any long-run speed or fuel effect is observed.

Atlas asset-cycle memory is refined because prolonged repair or conversion can alter charter availability, financing needs and secondhand value before a vessel becomes either fully productive or a recycling candidate.
The atlas already recalls retrofits, regulatory phase-outs and yard capacity as supply-side themes; P056 adds the project execution state machine rather than rediscovering those broad drivers.

Earlier Shipping passes already map condition surveys, casualty repair choices and end-of-life decisions. P056 composes those inputs inside planned repair/conversion execution without changing their semantic ownership.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Work scopes, commercial terms and schedule facts are project-specific and require authoritative project or company Evidence.
Technical findings, approval status and completion timing are vessel- and project-specific source facts.
Technical and statutory requirements depend on vessel configuration, rule vintage, flag/class and implementation details.
Provider identity, capability, current availability and rankings are source-first factual questions outside blind Memory.

stop_reason: The repair/life-extension lifecycle is populated from defect/worklist and repair decision through specification/tender/yard selection, docking/opening-up, parallel steel/machinery/equipment work, supplier/service dependencies, discovered-condition variations, conversion/retrofit integration, survey hold points, testing/trials and acceptance/redelivery/return to service. Further recall becomes specification-, quote-, contract-, price-, change-order-, duration-, finding-, test-, provider- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation and not technical, class, regulatory, safety, procurement or investment advice; no repair project, defect, work scope, quote, cost, duration, change order, equipment requirement, test result, approval, provider capability or redelivery date is verified.
